sections.h2: Ways to sell fast in Halfmoon
sections.html:
When time is short, a Halfmoon homeowner can hire an agent, go it alone, or sell straight to a cash buyer who accepts the property as it stands. Only the last option takes showings and repair work off the schedule. A house in good condition may bring a better price on the open market, though you'll wait months for it.

  • Agent listing: best for a tidy house when you can open the door for showings until the appraisal is done.
  • Selling alone: the commission stays with you, and so do pricing, contracts and transfer forms.
  • Cash purchase: a match for an estate, postponed repairs, a rental with tenants, or a tax or mortgage deadline.

Most local questions are about records: what the assessor holds, which permits were pulled, and where the deed is filed.

Halfmoon occupies the southeast corner of Saratoga County, with the Hudson on one side and the Mohawk on another. Population reached 26,658 in 2025, up 3.9% from the 2020 base, in 11,525 households averaging 2.27 people. Owners occupy 67.2% of homes and the median owner-occupied value is $387,700. Typical rent is $1,559, household income sits at $100,712, and the average commute takes 23.7 minutes. Before answering a cash offer, set it beside recent Halfmoon sales.

There's no single downtown here. The town is a set of hamlets, and lot size and frontage change a good deal between streets. Interstate 87, the Northway, forms the western edge. US 9 comes in over the Crescent Bridge across the Mohawk, US 4 serves the east, and NY 146 meets NY 236 near Newtown. People commuting to Albany usually ask about drive time first.

  • Crescent: in the south, where US 9 crosses the Mohawk.
  • Halfmoon hamlet: centered on County Roads 94, 95, 96 and 99.
  • Newtown: northeast, at NY 236, NY 146 and County Road 86.
  • Coons and Halfmoon Beach: one up north, one beside the river in the southwest.

Both the Erie Canal and the Champlain Canal once crossed town. A lot near an old canal route or the riverbank will draw questions from buyers about drainage and past flooding.

Halfmoon parcels pay school tax to Shenendehowa, Mechanicville or Waterford-Halfmoon, and the bill lists them alongside Saratoga County and assorted special districts. Look at the school line before you pick an asking price. Two neighbors split by a district boundary can see very different school bills. The town issues school bills in September and county bills in January.

The Assessment Office refreshes values each year and files the roll used by the county, the three school districts and the special districts. A full town-wide revaluation last finished in 1996, so assessments carry a long gap since the last complete reappraisal.

Value is fixed as of March 1, the taxable status date. Improvements completed afterward wait for the following cycle, and exemption applications are due on that same day. STAR won't appear on the roll because it is a credit, not an exemption.

Halfmoon assessment and tax calendar
DateWhat happens
March 1Taxable status date; exemption applications due
May 1Tentative roll filed; grievance forms accepted from this day
4th Tuesday of MayGrievance Day before the five-member Board of Assessment Review
July 1Final roll filed with Board of Assessment Review changes
September and JanuarySchool tax bills, then county tax bills

You can contest an assessment but not a tax bill, and a late filing gets dismissed. When a sale will close in spring, let the buyer know which step of this calendar the property has reached.

sections.h2: Permits and records to pull together
sections.html:
Your first stop is Building and Code Enforcement. It applies the state fire and building codes along with local laws and reviews construction drawings, and it wants owners to phone before starting work when a permit is in doubt.

A permit file in Halfmoon usually includes a plot plan showing distances to the property line, well and septic locations where they apply, three sets of plans and contractor insurance forms. A new driveway can need a curb cut permit from the Highway Department, NYS DOT or Saratoga County DPW, and some lots need a county sewer permit. Any addition, garage or finished basement will make the buyer's attorney ask for that paper trail.

  • Locate the plot plan and permits for each addition or outbuilding.
  • Check which school and special districts show on your bill.
  • Ask the Assessment Office which exemptions stop once title passes.
  • Note whether the house uses septic or sewer.

sections.h2: Recording the deed and paying transfer tax
sections.html:
Deeds go to the Saratoga County Clerk at 40 McMaster Street in Ballston Spa, which accepts land recordings until 4:15 in the afternoon. The office handles over 85,000 filings a year, from deeds to mortgages and discharges.

New York charges $2 on each $500 of the sale price, rounded up. Sellers normally pay it and file Form TP-584 with the deed no later than the 15th day after delivery. A buyer purchasing a residence for $1 million or more owes another 1%.

School and county bills land months apart, so the closing statement usually splits each by the days you owned the house. Check with the Assessment Office on any exemptions in place so the statement holds no surprises.

sections.h2: Steps from first call to closing
sections.html:
The sequence is short once you know where the records sit. First, pull your tax bill and note the school district and any special districts. Second, call the Assessment Office to learn which exemptions are on file and whether any will end at the sale. Third, gather permits and plot plans from Building and Code Enforcement for anything built after the house. Fourth, collect offers on paper and choose one with a closing date you can meet.

After that your attorney sends the contract, the buyer's side runs the title search, and the deed and Form TP-584 go to the Saratoga County Clerk. If the house is an estate property or has tenants, mention it at the start, since either one adds paperwork before title can pass.

sections.h2: What a cash sale skips and what it keeps
sections.html: No mortgage approval, no appraisal and no repair requests means a shorter schedule with a cash buyer. The title search, tax proration and deed filing all still take place. Before you sign, get the closing date, proof of funds and an itemized split of closing costs in writing, and let your attorney read the contract. A buyer who won't put those on paper is a poor bet, whatever the price.

faqs.q: Is a cash purchase in Halfmoon really quicker than a listing?
faqs.a: Typically, since there's no lender or appraisal between the offer and the deed. Title work and filing at the Saratoga County Clerk remain. Ask for the closing date in writing.

faqs.q: Must the roof or kitchen be repaired before a Halfmoon sale?
faqs.a: The law doesn't require repairs to sell. Cash buyers take the house in its present state. Unpermitted work is the real risk, so collect permits for additions from Building and Code Enforcement.

faqs.q: What does the seller owe the state at a Halfmoon closing?
faqs.a: Transfer tax of $2 per $500 of price. The buyer is liable only if the seller doesn't pay or is exempt, and the extra 1% on residences of $1 million or more falls on the buyer.

faqs.q: Can a Halfmoon owner dispute an assessment ahead of a sale?
faqs.a: Yes. File a complaint on the tentative roll between May 1 and Grievance Day, the fourth Tuesday of May, and the five-member Board of Assessment Review rules on the evidence. A tax bill itself can't be grieved.

faqs.q: Whose school tax will a Halfmoon buyer pay?
faqs.a: Shenendehowa, Mechanicville or Waterford-Halfmoon, depending on the parcel. The September bill is usually prorated at the closing.
